cards.stem: What running time does the source give for quicksort in the worst case?
cards.quote: Quicksort has running time Θ(n²) in the worst case, but it is typically O(n log n).
cards.hint: Recall the bound stated for the worst case.

cards.stem: What worst case bound does the source say a variant can achieve when always picking good pivots?
cards.quote: Select can be used to always pick good pivots, thus giving a variant with O(n log n) worst-case running time.
cards.hint: Think about the bound linked to always picking good pivots.

cards.stem: Which aspect is listed as varying among quicksort variants?
cards.quote: to select the pivot, to partition the array, to stop the recursion or switch to another algorithm for small partitions
cards.hint: Recall what variants differ in choosing.

cards.stem: What does the definition say is picked from the array to start quicksort?
options: Pick an element from the array (the pivot)
choose a random file from disk
cards.quote: Pick an element from the array (the pivot), partition the remaining elements into those greater than and less than this pivot
cards.hint: Remember the first step of the definition.
